newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Sinar Mas's AFP Singapore listing in July.
newsitem.headline: Sinar Mas's AFP Singapore listing in July.

text.p: Asia Food & Properties Ltd (AFP), the property, food processing and distribution arm of PT Sinar Mas Tunggal, hopes to list on the Stock Exchange of Singapore (SES) later this month, officials said on Friday.
"If everything goes well, the shares will be traded by 21 July, 1997 or earlier," Mak Lye Mun, head of corporate finance at OCBC Bank told a news conference.

OCBC is one of the three creditor banks including OUB Bank and the Bank of China which made an application for Singapore property and trading firm Amcol Holdings Ltd to be be placed under judicial management.
AFP acquired Amcol after it went into judicial management in July 1996 saying it could no longer service its debts.
Mak said AFP's listing in Singapore could be earlier if some logistical problems associated with its takeover of Amcol were solved.
These included making arrangements with Singapore's central depository board over some outstanding questions involving share swaps.
AFP's takeover of Amcol involved a share transfer scheme in which four new AFP shares were offered for every three Amcol shares, and one AFP warrant for every 10 offer shares held.

Following the share swaps, AFP owns 76.6 percent of its holding company, while existing Amcol shareholders hold 16.4 percent and Japanese trading houses Nissho Iwai and Itochu hold 1.7 percent and 5.3 percent respectively.
Hendrik Tee, AFP's director and chief executive officer, said the company expected to expand its property operations in future.
"Growth is expected to be spurred by Indonesia, which needs an estimated 1.9 million houses per year according to the government," Tee said.
AFP has some US$4.7 billion worth of property assets -- US$5.2 billion including Amcol's -- scattered throughout Asia and the United States.
For fiscal year ended December 31, 1996, AFP saw the bulk of its S$1.1 billion of turnover generated by its agribusiness and property division.
On future funding needs, officials said these would mostly be centred on expanding its food business in China. It could see a need for an additional US$125 million in funds, they said.
